issues.issue: Does issue estoppel bar the appellant from relitigating the employment issue (whether his parents' employment ended before his birth)?
issues.applicant_position: Issue estoppel is discretionary; new evidence not before the Board should let him relitigate the employment issue on its merits.
issues.result_quote: I find no reviewable error in this. Indeed, on this point I agree with the Federal Court’s reasons and conclusions.

issues.issue: Is judicial review premature because adequate and effective forums (Indian and Canadian citizenship routes) exist that the appellant must pursue first?
issues.applicant_position: Statelessness and Charter harms need immediate judicial review; the Minister is no adequate forum because he cannot consider the Charter.
issues.respondent_position: Minister says India and Canadian citizenship avenues are adequate forums the appellant must pursue first, so judicial review is premature.
issues.result_quote: Therefore, I uphold the preliminary objection that the appellant has other forums available to him that are adequate and effective.

issues.issue: Should the Court decide the constitutional and citizenship merits (Charter ss. 6 and 7, declaration of citizenship)?
issues.applicant_position: Charter ss. 6 and 7 and statelessness entitle him to a declaration of citizenship; the Federal Court should have granted it.
issues.respondent_position: Minister says administrative routes must come first; constitutional merits cannot yet be raised by way of judicial review.
issues.result_quote: I decline to offer any views concerning the merits of any application made to the Minister under subsection 5(4)
